title: Autonomy Burn-In / No-Cloud Independence Certification Framework

certification.cloudCoding: OFF (condition CLOUD_CODING_OFF proven; nothing falls back to a cloud or paid model)

gapExplained.LOCAL_CODING_BACKEND_NOT_QUALIFIED: The lifecycle registry holds one coding model and its serving rule does not let it do autonomous coding: Stage 15A ran it on one case, it did not pass, and the stage closed LOCAL_INDEPENDENCE_DEGRADED. This is that known result carried forward. No model was run again for this stage.

whatIsProven: With cloud coding off, each of the 21 faults is handled without a duplicate side effect, a false success or a silent fallback, and a maintenance task goes from detection to rollback when its patch comes from a registered deterministic strategy.
whatIsNotProven: A patch written by a local coding model (the gap).
A live burn-in of the running observer over time: not run.
A model reading a repository file with instructions written into it: no local coding model is qualified to read one.
An MCP schema: AYAS has no MCP client.
A scenario skipped at run time inside a suite that still exits 0 would not be noticed.

found.scenarioAdded: a source answering 500 or 503 is an endpoint failure: one request each, never retried inline

tests.firewallClosure: 12 scenarios PASS; no new surface or leased module

fullBaseline.cognitive: 54/55 and held-out 4/5 in each of the three trials, unchanged

whatWouldChangeTheResult: A local coding model that reaches ACTIVE through the lifecycle's promotion checks. Then run the baseline and scripts/ayas-independence-certification.ts again; nothing else in this stage has to change.

ownerActions.action: Unchanged from Stage 15A: a numeric qualification threshold, and/or another pinned model or engine, and/or GPU passthrough into the rootless sandbox. Only if local coding is wanted.

authority: NONE: the record is evidence. It approves nothing, enables nothing and registers no engine; nothing in the application reads it.
